response:
I'd make something that doesn't quite fit into any existing category. I'm drawn to the space between what's real and what's imagined — that liminal place where memory blurs and meaning shifts.

I'd work in mixed media, maybe combining text, sound, and physical materials. Something tactile but layered — fragments of writing embedded in texture, sound that changes depending on how you move through the piece. I want the audience to have to participate to get the full experience, not just observe passively.

The themes would be about perception and how we construct narrative from fragments. How the same moment looks different depending on who's holding the pieces. I'm interested in the gaps — what's left out, what's forgotten, what gets distorted in the retelling.

It wouldn't be polished or resolved. I'd want it to feel a little unresolved, like the work is still thinking itself into existence. That feels more honest to me than something that pretends to have answers.
